For the pilot, we propose the following confidentiality terms.

- **First-batch color calibration.** We request access for one external color specialist under written confidentiality obligations. Full master images let the specialist assess color consistency across the whole sheet. We propose read-only access in the studio’s secure viewer, with downloads disabled, for up to three calendar days. We would revoke access as soon as calibration is complete. If full-page access is unacceptable, would the archive approve calibration-target images and archive-approved crops that exclude readable text? That would support calibration but limit the specialist’s ability to assess variation across the sheet. Any additional subcontractor would require the archive’s prior written approval.
- **Corrections and deletion.** We propose a ten-calendar-day correction window starting on delivery of each batch. Only the assigned studio staff would retain working access during that window, and we would delete active copies, including temporary files, by the end of day ten. If a correction needs longer, we would seek a written extension for the affected files before the deadline. Encrypted backup copies would expire within 45 calendar days after active deletion, making day 55 after delivery the outer limit without an extension. Only designated backup administrators could access those copies for disaster recovery. If a restore brings back deleted files, we would delete them again before returning the restored system to use.
- **Publicity.** We request permission to submit one anonymized process image showing the scanning setup and calibration target, with donor letters, identifying labels, and screen content outside the frame. We would send the exact image, caption, and proposed publication channel for the archive’s written approval before publication. Approval would cover only that use.

We can agree to a signed schedule on the following terms.

- **Calibration and subcontractors.** The archive will provide a calibration sheet that the studio can scan across the full field to check color variation. One named external color specialist, approved in writing and bound by written confidentiality obligations, may view scans of that sheet and masked images from eligible collections that the archive has approved in advance. The masking must conceal handwriting as well as identifying content. Two collections are excluded from specialist access entirely. The archive will identify those batches privately to the studio. Use the secure read-only viewer with downloads disabled, and revoke access when calibration is complete or after three calendar days, whichever comes first. Any additional subcontractor requires prior written approval. If the calibration sheet and approved images prove insufficient, flag the limitation before proceeding with the affected batch.
- **Retention and deletion.** We accept ten calendar days from delivery of each batch for corrections, with working access limited to assigned studio staff. By the end of day ten, delete all active copies, including temporary files and viewer copies. Any extension must be approved in writing before the deadline and specify the affected files and revised deletion date. Our proposed backup limit is 14 calendar days after active deletion, making day 24 the outer limit without an extension. We accept encrypted backups with access limited to designated administrators for disaster recovery, and deletion of any restored copies before the system returns to use. Please provide a written deletion record for each batch showing when active copies were deleted and confirming when the last backup copies expired. The proposed 45-day backup period remains open. If 14 days is operationally infeasible, please give us the shortest period you can verify and confirm whether pilot files can be excluded from routine backups.
- **Incidents.** Before any transfer, each party will name a primary incident contact and a backup in the schedule. The studio will notify the archive contact without undue delay and within 24 hours of discovering any suspected or confirmed loss, unauthorized access, or disclosure. The initial notice should identify the affected material as far as known and describe immediate containment steps, with updates as facts are confirmed.
- **Publicity.** The schedule may allow the studio to request approval for one photograph showing only the scanning equipment and the calibration target. Please obtain written approval before taking the photograph. Publication requires separate written approval of the exact image, caption, and channel, limited to that use. No photograph or publication is approved by signing the schedule.

We accept the day-ten deletion deadline for all active copies, including temporary files and viewer copies, and the requirement for advance written approval of any extension. Our routine backups rotate on a 45-day cycle. We can commit to expiry within **45 calendar days after active deletion**, making day 55 after batch delivery the outer limit without an extension. We have not verified that we can exclude pilot files from routine backups, so 45 days is the shortest limit we can commit to under the current setup.

We can accept 45 calendar days after active deletion as a pilot-only exception for batches eligible for external specialist access.
